whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the Claude Certified Associate exam?

personas.label: Business Professionals
personas.description: You use Claude to draft content, summarize documents, or improve work processes without writing code.

personas.label: Team Leads Evaluating AI Tools
personas.description: You help choose or roll out AI tools and want to show that you understand prompts and responsible AI use.

personas.label: Career Changers Entering AI
personas.description: You come from a non-technical background and want to show that you can use generative AI at work.

examDifficulty.heading: Is the Claude Certified Associate exam hard?
examDifficulty.summary: CCAO-F is presented as an entry-level exam, but it still tests practical judgment. You need to spot incorrect answers, choose a suitable Claude model, and understand when sensitive data needs stronger controls.
bullets: 720/1000 passing score: you need consistent accuracy across all seven domains, not just strength in one area.
No coding required: The material is aimed at non-technical professionals. Practice with Claude each day before the exam.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: You may be ready when you can spot errors in Claude’s responses and explain why one prompt works better than another.

examFormat.heading: Claude Certified Associate exam format
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online. Here is what to expect:
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Most questions describe a team, a task, and a limit. Choose the approach that best meets the need. The exam focuses on how to use Claude, not memorizing definitions.
bestWayToPass: Use Claude each day for two weeks: Draft emails, summarize reports, compare options, and check each response.
Practice checking answers: Ask Claude questions where you know the answer, then verify each claim. This helps with the Response Quality section.
Choose products by use: Know when Claude.ai, Projects, the API, or Claude Code fits the team, task, and data sensitivity.
Use careful data controls: For confidential or regulated data, check the organization’s data rules and use the needed business controls.

certificationCard.description: Independent study notes and practice questions for Claude Certified Associate – Foundations. These materials are not an official Anthropic exam guide; we have not confirmed the credential’s availability or exam details with Anthropic.

keyConcepts.h2: Claude Certified Associate: Key Concepts for the Exam

blocks.heading: Writing Prompts That Get Reliable Results
blocks.body: Give Claude a clear task, useful background, and the format you want. Questions may describe work such as drafting a report summary, comparing vendors, or turning meeting notes into action items. Choose a prompt that gives enough information to produce a useful answer.

blocks.heading: Catching Mistakes in AI Output
blocks.body: Claude can make up facts, leave out important points, or give advice that conflicts with a source document. Decide whether to use the answer, correct it, or ask Claude to try again with better instructions or sources.

blocks.heading: Choosing the Right Claude Product and Model
blocks.body: Claude is available as a web and desktop app, a coding tool, an API, and a business product with team controls. The model options trade speed and cost against depth: Haiku is described as fast for high-volume tasks, Sonnet as a balance, and Opus for difficult reasoning or creative work.

blocks.heading: Setting Up Projects and Knowledge Sources
blocks.body: A Claude Project is a reusable workspace for instructions and reference files. Know how a Project differs from one conversation, how its files affect responses, and how to handle conflicts between Project instructions and a request in the conversation.

blocks.heading: Data Sensitivity and Responsible Use
blocks.body: Before sharing information with an AI tool, check how sensitive it is. Understand the data controls available in consumer and enterprise products, and know when a person should review a response before it reaches a customer.

scenarioTips.h2: How to pass the Claude Certified Associate exam
scenarioTips.intro: Questions describe a team, a task, and a limit, then ask what to do. Practice with Claude in daily work, and learn when its answers need more checking.

blocks.heading: Treat Prompts Like Mini-Briefs
blocks.body: Write a prompt like a short brief: state the goal, add context, and describe the output you need. Practice using examples and asking for step-by-step work. Good prompts give Claude the information it needs.

blocks.heading: Build Your Error-Spotting Instinct
blocks.body: Practice checking Claude’s answers. Ask about calculations, facts, and data comparisons where you know the expected result, then verify each claim.

blocks.heading: Map Each Product to a Use Case
blocks.body: Choose a product for the task: Claude.ai for occasional individual work; a shared Project for team instructions; the API for automated database workflows; Claude Code for development work.

blocks.heading: Know the Governance Boundaries
blocks.body: For confidential contracts, personal data, or regulated information, follow your organization’s data rules and use the needed enterprise safeguards. Prefer the option that limits exposure.

blocks.heading: Practice Across Real Workflows
blocks.body: Practice with real tasks for two weeks before taking the exam. Draft emails, summarize documents, compare options, and review each result.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Next Certifications After Claude Associate
nextCertsAfter.intro: After earning the Associate credential, advance to role-specific Claude certifications:

sampleQuestions.question: A marketing manager needs a launch email for three audience groups. What is the best prompt approach?
options: Give Claude product details and all three audiences, then request a tailored email for each
Write one generic email with no audience details, then customize each version by hand afterwards
Send three prompts without shared context
Ask Claude to write “email”
sampleQuestions.explanation: Give Claude the product details, describe each audience, and ask for a tailored version for each group.
whyWrong: Separate prompts without shared context may lead to inconsistent details.
A one-word prompt gives Claude no product, audience, or goal.

sampleQuestions.question: Claude gives a statistic and cites a 2024 McKinsey report. What should you do?
options: Accept it because it names a source
Check the report and statistic independently before using them
Remove the number but keep the citation, since the source itself is well known
Ask Claude to confirm its own answer
sampleQuestions.explanation: Claude can create plausible but false sources and statistics. Check the original source before using the claim.
whyWrong: A specific citation does not prove that a claim is true.
Keeping an unverified citation still presents it as a source.
Claude confirming its own answer is not independent verification.

sampleQuestions.question: A support team classifies 5,000 tickets a day and needs fast results. Which model tier fits best?
options: Opus, since its advanced capabilities suit every task
Sonnet because it is the default
Haiku for speed and lower cost on a repeated task
Any tier; they perform the same
sampleQuestions.explanation: Ticket classification is a clear, repeated task. Haiku is a good fit when speed and cost matter more than deep reasoning.
whyWrong: Opus may be more capable, but can be slower and cost more than this task needs.
Sonnet can work, but this high-volume task benefits more from speed and cost savings.
Model tiers differ in speed, cost, and capability.

sampleQuestions.question: A sales team wants Claude to review confidential customer contracts. What is the most responsible approach?
options: Paste the contracts into the free consumer product
Summarize every contract by hand first, then paste the summaries into any Claude product
Assume business documents have no privacy risks
Use business data controls and check each document against company policy
sampleQuestions.explanation: Use the appropriate business controls and check whether the organization’s data rules allow each document to be used with AI.
whyWrong: Consumer access may not have the controls required for confidential contracts.
Manual summaries may not scale and can still expose sensitive details.
Business documents can contain sensitive information and need protection.

sampleQuestions.question: What can a Claude Project do that a regular conversation cannot?
options: Keep reusable instructions and reference files for conversations in the workspace
Track organization billing and usage
Share conversations publicly
Train the model permanently on company data so that every future conversation remembers it
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Project stores instructions and reference files for use across conversations in that workspace.
whyWrong: Projects are not billing or usage reports.
Project setup does not make conversations public.
Project files do not permanently train or change the model.

sampleQuestions.question: You ask Claude for a Python script, but cannot check whether it is correct. What should you do?
options: Trust it because Claude is good at programming
Ask a developer to review it before use
Run it in production to see whether it works
Ask Claude if it is correct and proceed if it says yes
sampleQuestions.explanation: If you cannot check the code, ask a qualified developer to review it before running it in a production setting.
whyWrong: Programming ability does not guarantee every answer is correct.
Running unverified code in production can cause problems.
Claude cannot independently verify its own work.

sampleQuestions.question: A content team wants every blog post to use the same brand voice. Which feature helps most?
options: Set the same temperature value for every API call the team makes
Start each chat by saying “be creative”
Create a Project with brand instructions and style examples
Use a different model for each post
sampleQuestions.explanation: A Project keeps brand instructions and examples available across conversations in that workspace.
whyWrong: Temperature does not create shared brand guidance.
A vague instruction must be repeated and may not produce a consistent voice.
Using different models may make the style less consistent.

sampleQuestions.question: Why can asking Claude to “think step by step” sometimes improve an answer?
options: It limits the reply to three paragraphs
It joins separate conversations
It reduces the number of tokens used, so the answer arrives faster and costs less to produce
It can help Claude work through math, logic, or multi-part tasks before answering
sampleQuestions.explanation: Asking for steps can help with calculations, comparisons, and tasks with several parts by making the work easier to review.
whyWrong: This phrase does not set a paragraph limit.
It does not connect separate conversations.
Step-by-step answers often use more tokens, not fewer.

sampleQuestions.question: When is extended thinking worth the extra time and cost?
options: For difficult analysis, code review, or multi-step planning
For every prompt
For simple lookups and formatting tasks, where speed matters most
Only with the smallest model
sampleQuestions.explanation: Extended thinking can help on difficult tasks that need deeper reasoning. It may not help with a quick lookup or simple formatting.
whyWrong: Using it for every prompt can add time and cost without benefit.
Simple tasks do not usually need more reasoning time.
Model size alone does not determine whether extended thinking helps.

sampleQuestions.question: What most favors building a custom tool with the Claude API instead of using Claude.ai?
options: The team has no developers, needs a tool today, and wants to avoid any setup or maintenance work
The team must process many invoices automatically and send structured results to a database
One person uses Claude occasionally for ideas
The team wants a simple tool with no maintenance
sampleQuestions.explanation: The API fits automated, high-volume work that needs to send structured data to other systems. Claude.ai is better for occasional interactive tasks.
whyWrong: Without developers and with an immediate need, the Claude.ai interface may be easier.
One occasional user may not need a custom API tool.
A custom API tool needs development and maintenance.

sampleQuestions.question: A launch team needs a message tailored to three distinct audiences. What should the prompt provide?
options: Ask for one generic draft without describing the readers
Send separate prompts without shared product details or constraints
Give product facts and audiences, then request a tailored draft for each group
Request a launch email but provide no goal, audience, or product context
sampleQuestions.explanation: Provide product details, describe each audience, and request one tailored message for each group.
whyWrong: A generic draft lacks audience context needed to tailor the message.
Separate prompts can produce inconsistent facts and omit shared requirements.
The request omits the information Claude needs to produce a useful draft.

sampleQuestions.question: Claude cites a statistic from a report, but the number matters to a decision. What should the user do?
options: Check the original report and confirm the statistic before relying on it
Keep the citation because named sources make claims reliable
Ask Claude to repeat the claim and accept it if the wording is clear
Remove the number but keep the unverified report citation in the draft
sampleQuestions.explanation: Verify the statistic in the original report before relying on or sharing the claim.
whyWrong: A named citation does not show that the source or statistic is accurate.
A second answer from the same system is not independent verification.
An unverified citation can still mislead readers about the evidence.

sampleQuestions.question: A team classifies routine requests at high volume and needs low latency. Which model-selection approach fits?
options: Choose the most capable model for every request, regardless of need
Evaluate a fast, lower-cost model against the required quality threshold
Rotate model tiers randomly so requests receive varied responses
Use the slowest available tier to reduce the number of requests sent
sampleQuestions.explanation: Choose a fast, lower-cost model that meets the task’s quality threshold.
whyWrong: Using the highest-capability tier for a routine task may add needless cost or delay.
Random tier selection makes quality, latency, and cost less predictable.
A slower tier does not address the stated latency requirement.

sampleQuestions.question: A Project contains an outdated procedure, but a user asks for current guidance. What should the user do?
options: Assume the saved Project file is current because it is reusable
Ask Claude to infer the latest procedure from the old reference
Ignore the date and use the first matching paragraph in the file
Check an authoritative source, then refresh the Project reference
sampleQuestions.explanation: Check an authoritative current source and update or replace the outdated Project reference.
whyWrong: Reusable files can become stale and still need date and source checks.
An outdated reference cannot establish what the current procedure requires.
A matching paragraph may still describe a superseded process.

sampleQuestions.question: A team wants Claude to review confidential customer documents. What is the responsible first step?
options: Paste the documents into any available account to see what Claude finds
Remove customer names but ignore other identifying details and policy
Confirm policy and use an approved product with appropriate data controls
Assume business documents are safe to share because they are not public
sampleQuestions.explanation: Check company policy and use an approved product with the required data controls.
whyWrong: An unapproved account may not provide the organization’s required protections.
Other details can still identify people, and company rules still apply.
Confidential business documents can contain sensitive information.
